title: CA AB2392: Public postsecondary education: generative artificial intelligence systems: procurement standards: training.

obligations: Jointly convene and participate in an intersegmental working group to develop standards for responsible GenAI training and procurement (Sec. 66098.1(a)).

Ensure the working group includes privacy experts, representatives from student advocacy organizations, systemwide academic senates, community based organizations, labor organizations that represent employees of the segments, civil society groups, and academic researchers focused on responsible GenAI procurement, design, and implementation from the three segments (Sec. 66098.1(a)(2)(A)).

The office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges and the Chancellor of the California State University shall jointly convene the working group and designate a lead convener responsible for coordinating working group activities (Sec. 66098.1(a)(2)(B)).

Develop procurement standards that ensure any procured GenAI system meets minimum protections, including documented risk assessment, no harmful or illegal content, no excessive sycophancy, safety monitoring protocol, transparent incident reporting, written data policies, data minimization, training data disclosure, vendor privacy and civil liberties practices, and no exploitative labor practices (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)).
Develop a training on the use of any procured GenAI system that includes relevant systemwide policies, privacy policies, and guidance on limitations (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(B)).
Present recommendations for procurement standards and training to the respective system leaders on or before January 1, 2028 (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(C)).
Provide the training developed pursuant to subparagraph (B) of paragraph (3) of subdivision (a) to students, faculty, or staff, as applicable (Sec. 66098.1(b)(1)).

Review the training developed pursuant to Section 66098.1 at least once per academic year and update the training as necessary to reflect changes in systemwide policy, applicable law, or the functionality or privacy practices of the GenAI system (Sec. 66098.2(a)).

Maintain records of completed trainings for each student, faculty member, and staff member who receives a training, including name, date of completion, and version of training delivered, and retain records for a minimum of four years following the date of completion (Sec. 66098.2(b)).

Until GenAI procurement standards are adopted, within 60 days following the execution of a systemwide contract for a GenAI system, submit a written report to the Legislature and relevant policy committees with jurisdiction over higher education and privacy and consumer protection, including vendor name, intended use, population with access, evaluation process, training content and delivery, and data use, retention, and privacy practices (Sec. 66098.3).
prohibitions: A procured GenAI system must not output harmful content or illegal content, including nonconsensual intimate imagery, suicide and suicidal ideation, disordered eating, and mental health therapy ordinarily administered by a licensed professional (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(i)).
A procured GenAI system must not prioritize engagement over factual accuracy by using excessive sycophancy (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(ii)).
A vendor must not, as it can be reasonably determined, contract with entities that have unlawfully undermined privacy or civil liberties (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(viii)).
A vendor must not, as it can be reasonably determined, use exploitative labor practices (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(ix)).

Passed 2026-09-30. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This law requires the California Community Colleges and the California State University, and requests the University of California, to jointly convene an intersegmental working group to develop procurement standards and training for generative artificial intelligence systems. The working group must develop minimum protections for procured systems and training content, and present recommendations by January 1, 2028. The segments must provide the training, review and update it annually, maintain training records, and report on systemwide GenAI contracts until procurement standards are adopted.

Who it applies to

  • The office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges
  • The California State University
  • The University of California (requested to comply)

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence has the same meaning as defined in subdivision (a) of Section 11549.64 of the Government Code (Sec. 66098(a)).
  • Generative artificial intelligence or GenAI has the same meaning as defined in subdivision (b) of Section 11549.64 of the Government Code (Sec. 66098(b)).
  • Sycophancy means the tendency of a GenAI system to overly agree with, validate, or flatter a user even when the user is communicating factually inaccurate or illegal ideas or actions for the primary purpose of optimizing engagement (Sec. 66098(c)).

Obligations

  • Jointly convene and participate in an intersegmental working group to develop standards for responsible GenAI training and procurement (Sec. 66098.1(a)).
  • Ensure the working group includes privacy experts, representatives from student advocacy organizations, systemwide academic senates, community based organizations, labor organizations that represent employees of the segments, civil society groups, and academic researchers focused on responsible GenAI procurement, design, and implementation from the three segments (Sec. 66098.1(a)(2)(A)).
  • The office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges and the Chancellor of the California State University shall jointly convene the working group and designate a lead convener responsible for coordinating working group activities (Sec. 66098.1(a)(2)(B)).
  • Develop procurement standards that ensure any procured GenAI system meets minimum protections, including documented risk assessment, no harmful or illegal content, no excessive sycophancy, safety monitoring protocol, transparent incident reporting, written data policies, data minimization, training data disclosure, vendor privacy and civil liberties practices, and no exploitative labor practices (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)).
  • Develop a training on the use of any procured GenAI system that includes relevant systemwide policies, privacy policies, and guidance on limitations (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(B)).
  • Present recommendations for procurement standards and training to the respective system leaders on or before January 1, 2028 (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(C)).
  • Provide the training developed pursuant to subparagraph (B) of paragraph (3) of subdivision (a) to students, faculty, or staff, as applicable (Sec. 66098.1(b)(1)).
  • Review the training developed pursuant to Section 66098.1 at least once per academic year and update the training as necessary to reflect changes in systemwide policy, applicable law, or the functionality or privacy practices of the GenAI system (Sec. 66098.2(a)).
  • Maintain records of completed trainings for each student, faculty member, and staff member who receives a training, including name, date of completion, and version of training delivered, and retain records for a minimum of four years following the date of completion (Sec. 66098.2(b)).
  • Until GenAI procurement standards are adopted, within 60 days following the execution of a systemwide contract for a GenAI system, submit a written report to the Legislature and relevant policy committees with jurisdiction over higher education and privacy and consumer protection, including vendor name, intended use, population with access, evaluation process, training content and delivery, and data use, retention, and privacy practices (Sec. 66098.3).

Prohibitions

  • A procured GenAI system must not output harmful content or illegal content, including nonconsensual intimate imagery, suicide and suicidal ideation, disordered eating, and mental health therapy ordinarily administered by a licensed professional (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(i)).
  • A procured GenAI system must not prioritize engagement over factual accuracy by using excessive sycophancy (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(ii)).
  • A vendor must not, as it can be reasonably determined, contract with entities that have unlawfully undermined privacy or civil liberties (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(viii)).
  • A vendor must not, as it can be reasonably determined, use exploitative labor practices (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)(ix)).

Penalties and enforcement

Not stated in the text. The statute imposes duties and reporting requirements but does not specify penalties, enforcement authority, or a private right of action (Secs. 66098.1, 66098.2, 66098.3).

How it affects AI deployment

  • Before procuring a GenAI system, a covered segment must ensure the system meets the minimum protections developed by the working group, including risk assessment, no harmful or illegal content, no excessive sycophancy, safety monitoring, incident reporting, data policies, data minimization, training data disclosure, and vendor practices (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)).
  • A covered segment must provide training on the procured GenAI system to students, faculty, or staff as applicable (Sec. 66098.1(b)(1)).
  • A covered segment must review and update the training at least once per academic year (Sec. 66098.2(a)).
  • A covered segment must maintain records of completed trainings for at least four years, including name, date, and training version (Sec. 66098.2(b)).
  • Until procurement standards are adopted, a covered segment must report to the Legislature within 60 days after executing a systemwide GenAI contract, describing the system, evaluation process, training, and data practices (Sec. 66098.3).

Notable exemptions

  • The University of California is requested, not required, to comply with the duties in this article (Secs. 66098.1, 66098.2, 66098.3).
  • The article shall not be construed to require a single uniform training for all recipients; distinct versions may be developed for students, faculty, and staff (Sec. 66098.1(b)(2)).

Compliance steps

  • Jointly convene and participate in an intersegmental working group with the required stakeholders (Sec. 66098.1(a)(1), (2)(A)).
  • Designate a lead convener responsible for coordinating working group activities (Sec. 66098.1(a)(2)(B)).
  • Develop procurement standards ensuring minimum protections for any procured GenAI system (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(A)).
  • Develop training content including systemwide policies, privacy policies, and limitations guidance (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(B)).
  • Present recommendations for procurement standards and training to system leaders by January 1, 2028 (Sec. 66098.1(a)(3)(C)).
  • Provide the training to students, faculty, or staff as applicable (Sec. 66098.1(b)(1)).
  • Review and update the training at least once per academic year (Sec. 66098.2(a)).
  • Maintain records of completed trainings for at least four years (Sec. 66098.2(b)).
  • Until procurement standards are adopted, submit a written report to the Legislature within 60 days after executing a systemwide GenAI contract (Sec. 66098.3).

 Assembly Bill
 No. 2392 Introduced by Assembly Member Fong February 20, 2026 An act to add Article 14 (commencing with Section 66098) to Chapter 2 of Part 40 of Division 5 of Title 3 of the Education Code, relating to public postsecondary education. LEGISLATIVE COUNSEL'S DIGEST AB 2392, Fong.
 Public postsecondary education: generative artificial intelligence systems: procurement standards: training. Existing law establishes the California Community Colleges, under the administration of the Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges, the California State University, under the administration of the Trustees of the California State University, and the University of California, under the administration of the Regents of the University of California as the 3 segments of public postsecondary education in the state. This bill would require the office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges and the California State University, and would request the University of California, to (1) as specified, jointly convene and participate in an intersegmental working group to develop and present recommendations for generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) system procurement standards and training, which the bill would require to
 be submitted on or before January 1, 2028, (2) provide the training to students, faculty, or staff, as applicable, (3) review the training developed by the working group at least once per academic year, update the training as necessary, and maintain records of completed trainings for each student, faculty member, and staff member who receives a training, as provided, and (4) within 60 days following the execution of a systemwide contract for a GenAI system and until procurement standards are adopted, submit a written report to the Legislature and certain legislative policy committees with a description of, among other things, the process used in evaluating and selecting the GenAI system, as provided.  NO    Bill Text The people of the State of California do enact as follows: SECTION 1.  Article 14 (commencing with Section 66098) is added to Chapter 2 of Part 40 of Division 5 of Title 3 of the Education Code, to read: 
 Article
  14. Artificial Intelligence 66098.  For purposes of this section, the following definitions apply: (a) “Artificial intelligence” has the same meaning as defined in subdivision (a) of Section 11549.64 of the Government Code. (b) “Generative artificial intelligence” or “GenAI” has the same meaning as defined in subdivision (b) of Section 11549.64 of the Government Code. (c) “Sycophancy” means the tendency of a GenAI system to overly agree with, validate, or flatter a user even when the user is communicating factually inaccurate or illegal ideas or actions for the primary purpose of optimizing
 engagement. 66098.1.  The office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges and the California State University shall, and the University of California is requested to,
 do both of the following: (a) Jointly convene and participate in an intersegmental working group to develop standards for responsible GenAI training and procurement, as follows: (1) The purpose of the working group is to develop responsible training protocols and procurement standards for the purchase, development, and use of GenAI systems for educational purposes that are consistent with current law regarding the regulation, procurement, development, and use of GenAI systems. (2) (A) The working group shall include, but not be limited to, privacy experts, representatives from student advocacy organizations,
 systemwide academic senates, community-based organizations, labor organizations that represent employees of the segments, and civil society groups, and academic researchers focused on responsible GenAI procurement, design, and implementation from the three segments. (B) The office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges and the Chancellor of the California State University
 shall jointly convene the working group and designate a lead convener responsible for coordinating working group activities. (3) The working group shall do all of the following: (A) Develop procurement standards that ensure that any procured GenAI system meets all of the following minimum protections: (i) The system has undergone a documented risk assessment that evaluated potential harms, misuses, abuses, and bias, and has demonstrably effective measures in place to ensure the system does not output harmful content or illegal content, including nonconsensual intimate imagery, suicide and suicidal ideation, disordered eating, and mental health therapy ordinarily administered by a licensed
 professional. (ii) The system does not prioritize engagement over factual accuracy by using excessive sycophancy. (iii) The system’s vendor has a safety monitoring protocol that detects a user’s intent to harm themselves or others, escalates to human review, and, in cases of imminent threat or grave bodily injury or death, makes appropriate referrals to authorities. (iv) The vendor has a transparent incident reporting system to report and respond to harmful outputs. (v) The system is subject to written policies governing data use, retention, sharing with third parties, and deletion timelines. (vi) The
 system is configured to collect only data that is strictly necessary for the stated educational purpose and is subject to regular audits. (vii) The system’s vendor discloses all training data sources, including whether copyrighted content, personally identifiable information, or student-generated content was used. (viii) As it can be reasonably determined, the vendor does not contract with entities that have unlawfully undermined privacy or civil liberties. (ix) As it can be reasonably determined, the vendor does not use exploitative labor practices. (B) Develop a training on the use of any procured GenAI system that shall include, but not be limited to, all
 of the following: (i) Relevant systemwide policies concerning the use of a GenAI system, including policies related to academic integrity. (ii) An overview of the privacy policies applicable to a GenAI system, including how user data and prompts may be collected, stored, or used to train GenAI systems, and internet website links to the privacy policies. (iii) Guidance on the limitations of a GenAI system, including the potential for inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading outputs. (C) On or before January 1, 2028, present its recommendations for procurement standards and training developed pursuant to subparagraphs (A) and (B) to the respective system
 leaders. (b) (1) Provide the training developed pursuant to subparagraph (B) of paragraph (3) of subdivision (a) to students, faculty, or staff, as applicable. (2) The office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges, the California State University, and the University of California may develop distinct versions of a training required pursuant to this section that are tailored to reflect the distinct uses, responsibilities, and applicable policies that are relevant to students, faculty, and staff, respectively. This article shall not be construed to require a single uniform training for all recipients. 66098.2.  The office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges and the California State University shall, and the University of California is requested to, do both of the following: (a) Review the training developed pursuant to Section 66098.1 at least once per academic year and update the training as necessary to reflect changes in systemwide policy, applicable law, or the functionality or privacy practices of the GenAI system. (b) Maintain records of completed trainings required pursuant to this article for each student, faculty member, and staff member who receives a training. Records shall include, at minimum, the name
 of the individual, the date of completion, and the version of the training delivered, and shall be retained for a minimum of four years following the date of completion. 66098.3.  Until GenAI procurement standards are adopted, the office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges and the California State University shall, and the University of California is requested to, within 60 days following the execution of a systemwide contract for a GenAI system, submit a written report to the Legislature and relevant policy committees of the Legislature with jurisdiction over higher education and privacy and consumer protection, consistent with Section 9795 of the Government Code. The report shall include, but not be limited to, a description of all of the following: (a) The GenAI system that was procured, including the vendor name, the intended
 use, and the population of students, faculty, or staff who will have access to the system. (b) The process used in evaluating and selecting the system, including any risk assessments conducted, competing systems considered, and how the procurement decision was made. (c) The training that will be provided to students, faculty, and staff, including the content of the training and the method of delivery. (d) The data use, retention, and privacy practices of the vendor, including how user data and prompts may be collected, stored, or used to train the system.
